title: A sky photo is expected to appear in Memories
preconditions: A adds a photo in Us.
B expects every shared photo to appear in Memories.
Neither has read the explanation of the two destinations.

actions.note: A chooses a photo for the sky.
B searches Memories for the same photo.

expected_behavior: The app makes clear that a sky photo and a dated memory are separate actions.
A sky photo does not silently become a dated memory.
The archive remains the complete place to browse dated content.
candidate_failure_modes: B concludes the photo failed to save.
A believes one action published to both destinations.
The app adds a second, unrequested copy to resolve the ambiguity.

observed_code_behavior: Us and Memories are intentionally separate destinations; sky photos are not dated memories.
Free and Plus see the same relationship home.

hypothetical_user_behavior:
A fictional participant (Jules Park) said: "Ran this audit against my own restores, mostly on bad train wifi. My three, and the one I'd keep:

1. The recovery phrase "check" screen. It exists because we don't trust the write-down, so we make the user prove it — but the phrase was already checksummed. Cost: a 12-word retype on a keyboard that autocorrects. Remove: nothing breaks, the checksum already rejects bad input. The check screen is a feeling, not a guard.

2. The device list, shown during restore. At that exact moment the list is the archive describing a sky that isn't there yet — the current device isn't in it and the old one is lying. Keep the list in settings, where it's true. Delete it from the restore path.

3. The helper line explaining trust codes, rendered inside the enrollment warning. Two explanations of one thing in one dialog means one of them is decoration. Decoration that hides state is worse than no state.

Keep: the destructive warning before enrollment that says the old device loses access. It's the only line I read twice, and the only one that changed what I did. That's the test — if a line can't be acted on, it isn't help, it's delay."
Jules Park assumes: the sky is not the archive
Jules Park assumes: a setting applies immediately
Mina Sol assumes: a heading is a heading
Mina Sol assumes: a button that looks disabled is disabled
